name: Field Doctor-Style Vegetable Korma (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
465 g Whole grain rice
3 1/2 medium Sweet Potatoes
360 g Potato
200 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
200 g Spinach
3/4 medium Aubergines
1 1/2 medium Carrots
95 g Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
1/4 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
75 g Red Quinoa
75 g Tomato Puree [tomato]
1 1/4 Lemon Juice
2 1/2 tbsp Ginger
2 1/2 tbsp Pumpkin Seed
4 tbsp Coriander
3/4 tbsp Brown Sugar
1 tbsp Tapioca Starch
1 tsp Sea Salt
1 1/4 tsp Turmeric
1 1/4 tsp Cumin Ground
1 tsp Coriander Ground
1/2 tsp Cinnamon Ground
2/3 tsp Fennel Ground
1/2 tsp Dried Fenugreek Ground
1/2 tsp Green Cardamon Ground
1/2 tsp Nutmeg Ground
1/2 tsp Saffron
directions:
1. Grains: Cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa until tender; drain and keep warm.

2. Roast veg: Toss cubed sweet potato, potato, aubergine and carrot with a little extra virgin olive oil and roast at 200°C until soft and lightly coloured.

3. Korma sauce: Warm extra virgin olive oil with ginger, then add turmeric, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, fenugreek, cardamom, nutmeg and a pinch of saffron. Stir in soy milk, coconut milk, chopped tomato, tomato puree, lemon juice and brown sugar. Simmer gently; thicken with tapioca slurry if needed. Season with salt.

4. Finish: Fold roasted vegetables and spinach into the sauce until the spinach wilts. Serve over rice–quinoa with coriander and pumpkin seeds.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Whole grain rice, Sweet Potato, Potato, Soy Milk [SOY beans, water], Spinach, Aubergine, Carrot...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Vegetable Korma (Low FODMAP) (~398 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/sweet-potato-spinach-korma
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~398 g x 8 = 3184 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~523 g (inferred ~16.43% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~94 g (inferred ~2.96% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
